narrative:
The model estimated a 34.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk—roughly a one-in-three chance. The lender treats that level as above its acceptable risk limit, so your application was denied even though the estimate is below half.

The decision was influenced most by your credit history, then by your checking-account status, and then by the amount requested. Your credit history was the single strongest factor and, in your case, it actually leaned toward good credit rather than against you. However, the next two factors pushed the other way. Your checking-account status was 0–200 DM, a category seen among only 18.4% of approved applicants, and it increased the perceived risk. The requested amount—8,386 DM compared with an approved average of about 3,020 DM—also pushed toward bad credit because it is much larger than typical approved requests.

To improve your position, focus on reducing the amount requested and building a stronger checking-account balance before reapplying. You should also review your credit history for any unresolved critical or delayed items and ask the lender what specific balance or loan size would meet its criteria.
